name: UC Davis
summary: UC Davis main campus in Davis, CA with on-site substation power, large student housing areas, and reliance on UC Davis Medical Center in Sacramento for inpatient care.

power.utility: UC Davis (own 115 kV Main Substation for most areas); PG&E for Cuarto and some apartments
power.how_it_is_fed: Campus manages high-voltage distribution from its 115 kV Main Substation fed by grid electricity supplemented by on-site solar farm and hydropower contracts. Some residence areas receive PG&E supply.

buildings.name: 115 kV Main Substation
buildings.why: Primary on-campus electrical substation serving nearly all core campus facilities.

buildings.name: Davis Substation
buildings.why: Electrical substation operated by Pacific Gas and Electric Company, about 1715 m from the centre of campus. From OpenStreetMap.

buildings.name: UC Davis Medical Center
buildings.why: Nearest hospital with inpatient beds and emergency department, located approximately 15 miles (20-minute drive) south in Sacramento.

buildings.name: Tercero - Campbell Hall
buildings.why: One of the largest residence halls in the Tercero area housing hundreds of students.

buildings.name: Segundo Bixby Hall
buildings.why: Major residence hall in the Segundo area serving large numbers of residents.

buildings.name: Cuarto - Tahoe Hall
buildings.why: Key building in the Cuarto residence hall complex with significant student population.

buildings.name: Regan Central Commons (Main)
buildings.why: Main building of the Regan residence halls complex for large resident capacity.

buildings.name: Peter J. Shields Library
buildings.why: Main campus library serving as central academic resource for students and faculty.

buildings.name: Memorial Union
buildings.why: Primary student union and gathering hub on campus.

buildings.name: Fire & Police Building
buildings.why: Headquarters for campus police and public safety operations.

buildings.name: Genome & Biomedical Sciences Facility
buildings.why: Major research building supporting biomedical and genomic studies.

buildings.name: Earth and Physical Sciences Building
buildings.why: Large classroom and laboratory building for sciences.

buildings.name: Mathematical Sciences Building
buildings.why: Significant classroom and academic building for math and related fields.

buildings.name: Social Sciences & Humanities Building
buildings.why: Large classroom building central to humanities and social sciences instruction.

buildings.name: Hart Hall
buildings.why: Key classroom and academic building on the central campus.

buildings.name: Memorial Union Unitrans Terminal
buildings.why: Primary transit hub with Unitrans bus terminal connecting campus buildings.

buildings.name: Silo Unitrans Terminal
buildings.why: Secondary major transit terminal serving campus routes.

transit.name: Unitrans A Line
transit.connects: Memorial Union Terminal to Segundo and Tercero housing areas

transit.name: Unitrans B Line
transit.connects: Memorial Union Terminal to Silo and central academic buildings

transit.name: Unitrans C Line
transit.connects: Silo Terminal to research and south campus buildings

placement.note: Positions come from OpenStreetMap. Which building is on which feed is assumed: each is put on its nearest power source.
